source_neutral.procedure: The work starts from an explicit set of competing explanations for the reported checkout latency regression and a table that cross-references evidence against those explanations. Using available version and configuration history, each plausible deployed change is listed as a candidate explanation. The list also includes load variation alone, interactions between a change and load, combinations of changes, and dependency or measurement changes where plausible. All entries are held as proposed explanations, not established causes. The procedure assumes that deployment identities, traffic strata, traces and latency measurements can be recovered; missing information and uncertain assumptions are recorded as such and are not treated as facts. The overall process is: fix definitions, score every evidence item against every explanation, run controlled comparisons where feasible and safe, enter those results into the same table, test how sensitive the rankings are to evidence and assumption choices, and either attribute a bounded contribution or report an unresolved set of explanations.
source_neutral.action: 1) Define the latency outcome, the comparison window, and the relevant traffic and configuration strata before comparing candidates. 2) Build a table with explanations as columns and evidence items as rows. 3) Score every timeline, trace, latency-distribution and resource-counter observation against every explanation as consistent, inconsistent or uninformative, recording a rationale and a reliability assessment for each. 4) Keep missing evidence distinct from contradiction; give weight to reliable contradictions that separate alternatives and do not tally supporting items. 5) Where feasible, replay representative checkout workloads in staging while changing one candidate revision or configuration at a time. 6) Compare candidate present versus candidate absent at matched load, and vary load with the candidate held fixed; repeat the comparisons to assess variability. 7) If bundled changes remain indistinguishable, apply revision bisection. 8) If staging leaves material ambiguity, consider production rollback and controlled reintroduction, and do so only when safe, with latency and resource abort thresholds and a recovery action defined in advance; if a threshold is crossed, stop the experiment and restore the safer state. 9) Enter test results into the same table, scored against all explanations. 10) Reassess the rankings after removing unreliable evidence, treating dependent observations as a single evidence group, varying the judgments of how discriminating each item is, and changing uncertain assumptions. 11) If alternatives remain tied, seek a trace or controlled comparison on which their predictions differ.
source_neutral.observables: The proposed signal is a comparative pattern across the whole table, not a deployment timestamp alone. Specific patterns: (a) a repeatable latency difference between candidate-present and candidate-absent runs at matched load would contradict load variation alone, within those conditions; (b) a latency increase as load rises with the revision held fixed could support a load explanation, but would not by itself exclude a contribution from a deployed change; (c) an effect confined to high load could support a change-load interaction; (d) traces and resource counters could distinguish mechanisms where the explanations predict different behavior for them; (e) disappearance of the regression on rollback and recurrence on controlled reintroduction would be discriminating only to the extent that load, configuration, dependencies and measurement remain comparable. No such observations are supplied in the packet; all of these are anticipated, not recorded, signals.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: Explanations with important, reliable contradictions are weakened or conditionally eliminated; explanations that survive the full comparison and the sensitivity checks are retained. A bounded causal contribution is attributed to a particular change only if all three hold: controlled contrasts isolate that change, the observed difference exceeds the assessed run-to-run variability, and plausible competing explanations fare worse. If established, the report states the change identity, the latency effect, and the tested workload and configuration scope, and identifies a load interaction where supported. If only timing aligns, the result is reported as a candidate association. If several explanations survive, or if the rankings depend on uncertain evidence, the result is reported as unresolved alternatives and no unique cause is named. A surviving explanation is not treated as proven true.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: (1) candidate explanations — each plausible deployed change, load variation alone, change-load interactions, combinations of changes, and dependency or measurement changes where plausible; (2) evidence items — timeline, trace, latency-distribution and resource-counter observations, plus results of staging and production tests; (3) definitional frame — latency outcome, comparison window, traffic and configuration strata; (4) recorded gaps and uncertain assumptions. Relationships: each evidence item is related to each explanation by a score of consistent, inconsistent or uninformative, with a rationale and reliability rating; dependent observations are grouped as one evidence unit; controlled contrasts are organized along two axes — candidate present versus absent at matched load, and load varied with the candidate fixed — so that change effects, load effects and their interaction can be separated; bundled changes are subdivided by revision bisection when they cannot otherwise be distinguished; rankings of explanations are linked to evidence reliability, discrimination judgments and assumptions through the sensitivity reassessment.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: Specified follow-up: if staging leaves material ambiguity, consider production rollback and controlled reintroduction under the stated safety conditions; if bundled changes remain indistinguishable, use revision bisection; if alternatives remain tied after reassessment, seek a trace or a controlled comparison on which the tied explanations predict different outcomes. If limitations undermine discrimination, narrow the claim and keep the affected alternatives under consideration. No further follow-up beyond these steps is specified.
source_neutral.limits: Conditions and assumptions: deployment identities, traffic strata, traces and latency measurements are assumed recoverable; staging replay and single-change variation are done where feasible; production rollback and reintroduction are considered only when safe and only with predefined latency and resource abort thresholds and a recovery action. Stopping rules: a production experiment is stopped and the safer state restored if an abort threshold is crossed; attribution stops at an unresolved set of explanations if no safe, feasible discriminating test remains. Sources of distortion in the table: incomplete candidate lists, deployments coupled together, shared assumptions, correlated telemetry, unreliable measurements, and subjective judgments of how discriminating an item is. Matched-load comparisons assume the relevant conditions are sufficiently comparable. Staging results depend on how representative the workload and environment are. Rollback may also alter caches or other state, which limits isolation of the code change. A surviving explanation is not proven true. A tested causal contribution need not account for the entire production regression and need not generalize beyond the tested conditions. Where these limitations undermine discrimination, the claim is narrowed and the affected alternatives are retained. No observations are supplied in the packet, so no attribution is made here.
